definition: Defunct means no longer used or existing.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word defunct. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know defunct should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The city's pneumatic-tube mail system, defunct since the 1950s, still threads beneath the streets like the fossil of a faster idea.
A fading business still opens its doors, though fewer people walk through them; defunct means the doors have closed for good.
Forgotten goes even further than defunct: a defunct railroad can still be mourned and mapped, but a forgotten one has vanished from memory as well as from the timetable.

Extinct is the ending biology reserves for species and natural kinds — the last member has died, and the world holds no more. Defunct does the same certifying work for human creations: leagues, airlines, journals, brands. The passenger pigeon is extinct; the railway that carried its hunters is defunct.

Discontinued means a maker chose to stop producing something — a model, a flavor, a product line — while the company itself sails on. Defunct reaches further: the enterprise has ceased to exist. A discontinued sedan still has a manufacturer; a defunct automaker has nothing left to discontinue.

Chasing a 1979 route over the Alps, the historian needed an article from Freewheel, a cycling weekly that once outsold the national dailies every July.
The magazine is defunct: its publisher liquidated in 1983, the presses were sold, and the title has belonged to no one for forty years.
This was no quiet trimming of a catalog — the company itself ceased to exist, owing money and holding one last unprinted issue.
Nor did it linger half-alive; there was no shrinking subscriber list, only a Tuesday when the office simply did not open.
What survives is paper: bound volumes in three libraries, which is where the historian finally found her route.
